intro: This page explains how Luca's pricing is structured: what you pay for, what does not change your price and how billing works. It is for founders and finance leads comparing Luca with other analytics tools or with hiring an analyst.
It describes the pricing model only. For current plans and figures, see ask-luca.com/pricing, and for what happens when you sign up, see Trial and signup.

sections.title: What this page covers
paragraphs: This page covers the pricing model: seat-based pricing, usage, integration fees, annual billing and how to think about cost against hiring. It does not list plan names, prices, discount sizes or trial terms, because those change.
Plans and prices are published on ask-luca.com/pricing, and you can read them there without a sales call. Check that page before you budget.

sections.title: The model at a glance
paragraphs: Luca prices by seat. Store revenue, order volume and ad spend do not set the price, so the plan price does not rise as your brand grows.

Every plan lists unlimited usage. The website states that custom connectors carry no integration fee, and annual billing is offered at a discount to monthly billing. The size of that discount is shown on ask-luca.com/pricing.

intro: This page describes what happens when you sign up for Luca, so you can prepare before you start. It is for the person who will create the account and connect the first data source.
Trial availability and terms are not covered here. Check ask-luca.com/pricing for the current offer, and see Onboarding for what Luca's team does with you after signup.

sections.title: What this page covers
paragraphs: This page covers the signup sequence: creating an organisation, connecting data and entering card details. It does not state trial length, plan prices or when a card is charged. Confirm those on ask-luca.com/pricing.

sections.title: What to have ready
paragraphs: Signup includes creating an organisation before you connect data, and it asks for a data connection and card details up front.
Before you begin, decide which platform you will connect first and make sure you can sign in to it. Have the card you plan to bill to ready.

intro: This section explains where Luca stores your data, who processes it, what access Luca requests and what happens to your data when you leave. It is for founders, finance leads and anyone completing a vendor security review.
Luca connects to your commerce, advertising, analytics, payments and accounting systems, so this is the place to check what happens to that data once it is connected.

sections.title: In this section
paragraphs: Data handling covers hosting on Google Cloud Platform, the separate dataset each customer's data sits in, how credentials are kept, the sub-processors named in the privacy policy and Luca's position on AI model training.
Access and deletion covers read-only access scopes and what happens to your data after you disconnect a platform or close your account.

sections.title: Security reviews and documentation
paragraphs: These pages summarise what Luca's privacy policy and website state. They are not a substitute for a formal review, and the privacy policy at ask-luca.com/privacy holds the binding wording.
If your process needs certification details, a completed security questionnaire or further security documentation, request it from Luca's team.

intro: This page explains where Luca hosts your data, how each customer's data is kept separate, which sub-processors handle it and whether it is used to train AI models. It is for anyone assessing Luca as a vendor.
It summarises Luca's privacy policy and website. For access scopes and deletion, see Access and deletion.

sections.title: What this page covers
paragraphs: This page covers hosting, the separation of customer data, credential storage, named sub-processors and model training. It reflects ask-luca.com/privacy and ask-luca.com as read on 16 October 2026.
It does not cover certifications. Ask Luca's team for security documentation, or about anything your review needs that is not listed here.

sections.title: Summary
paragraphs: Infrastructure runs on Google Cloud Platform. Each customer's data sits in a separate BigQuery dataset, and credentials are kept in Google Secret Manager.

The privacy policy names OpenAI and Google Cloud Platform as sub-processors. OpenAI processes data under enterprise terms that exclude training on it, and the website states that Luca does not train third-party foundation models on customers' financials.

intro: This page explains the level of access Luca requests when you connect a platform, and what happens to your data after you disconnect or close your account. It is for the person approving connections and for anyone reviewing data retention.
For hosting, data separation and sub-processors, see Data handling.

sections.title: What this page covers
paragraphs: This page covers access scopes, deletion and retention. Read-only scopes are published for Google connections. Scopes for other connectors are shown on each platform's own permission screen when you connect.
Retention periods for data other than Google data are set out in the privacy policy at ask-luca.com/privacy, not on this page.

sections.title: Checking access when you connect
paragraphs: When you connect a platform, read the permission screen that platform shows before you approve. For connectors other than Google, that screen is where you see what Luca is requesting.

intro: This section explains how Luca's team helps you get set up and where you can learn from other users. It is for teams planning a rollout and for anyone who wants to know what working with Luca looks like after signup.
Onboarding with Luca is done with you: Luca's team does much of the setup work, including data mapping and reconciling your systems into Numbers.

sections.title: In this section
paragraphs: Onboarding describes the hands-on setup Luca's team runs for each client, including custom connectors, integration mapping and reconciliation into Numbers, and how onboarding capacity is managed by intake.
Community and podcast describes the Luca community on Heartbeat and the E-Commerce Leaders Series podcast.

sections.title: Company and customers
paragraphs: For the people behind Luca, see About. For the brands shown on Luca's website, see Customers.

Onboarding is where your connected systems are mapped and reconciled into Numbers, Luca's reconciled view of your figures.

If your start date matters, ask Luca's team which intake you would join before you sign up.

Both sit alongside the onboarding Luca's team runs with you.

sections.title: What this page covers

Luca is an AI analyst agent for e-commerce brands. For how your data is handled, see the Security section.

Testimonials are not reproduced in this documentation. Read them on ask-luca.com.

Named testimonials with photographs from leaders at Ayodi, Untamed and Nidra are published on ask-luca.com.

parameters.name: Customer data kept separate
parameters.definition: Tenant isolation is the practice of storing each customer's data apart from other customers' data in a shared service.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is how a service used by many customers keeps one customer's data apart from another's. It is a standard question in a vendor review.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Each customer's data sits in its own BigQuery dataset on Google Cloud Platform.
Credentials you provide when you connect platforms are kept in Google Secret Manager. Both points are stated in Luca's privacy policy at ask-luca.com/privacy.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps you answer the data separation question in a vendor review with a specific storage model rather than a general assurance.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Without a stated separation model, you would need to ask how your data is stored relative to other customers before you could complete a review.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Founders, finance leads and anyone completing a security or vendor questionnaire for their brand.

parameters.example: During setup or a trial, ask your reviewer to read the dataset and credential statements in the privacy policy. Then send Luca's team any follow-up questions your questionnaire requires and record their answers alongside the policy wording.
parameters.boundary: This describes how data is stored. It is not a certification or audit result. Request security documentation from Luca's team if your review needs it.
parameters.review: Confirm the wording matches the current privacy policy, and decide whether to attach an architecture diagram or security documentation.

parameters.name: Your data is not used to train AI models
parameters.definition: A no-training commitment states that the data you give a service is not used to train AI models.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is a statement about whether the data you connect is used to train or improve AI models beyond your own use of the service.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca uses OpenAI as its language model provider, and OpenAI processes data under enterprise terms that exclude training on it.
Luca's website also states that Luca does not train third-party foundation models on customers' financials.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps you assess whether to connect financial data, since model training is a common concern in vendor reviews.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Without a stated position, a reviewer would need to establish whether your financials could be used for model training before approving a connection.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Founders, finance leads and reviewers responsible for sensitive financial data.

parameters.example: Before you connect your accounting system, read the training statements in the privacy policy and on ask-luca.com. Ask Luca's team how you can review the enterprise terms referenced, and check them against your internal data policy.
parameters.boundary: The statements cover OpenAI's processing under enterprise terms and Luca not training third-party foundation models on customers' financials. Ask Luca's team about anything outside those statements.
parameters.review: Confirm the exact website wording, and whether Luca can share the OpenAI enterprise terms or a summary of them.

parameters.name: Sub-processors disclosed
parameters.definition: A sub-processor is a third party that processes customer data on a vendor's behalf. Disclosure means the vendor names them publicly.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is a published list of the third parties that handle your data for a vendor.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca's privacy policy names two sub-processors: OpenAI, the language model provider, and Google Cloud Platform, which runs Luca's infrastructure.
You can read the list at ask-luca.com/privacy.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps you complete the third-party section of a vendor review and check each named provider against your own policies.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Without a published list, you would need to request one before you could assess where your data goes.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Reviewers, legal teams and finance teams handling data protection checks.

parameters.example: Open the privacy policy and compare the named sub-processors with your approved vendor list. If your process requires a sub-processor agreement or notice of changes, ask Luca's team how they handle it.
parameters.boundary: This reflects the privacy policy as read on 16 October 2026. Check the live policy for the current list.
parameters.review: Confirm the list is complete, and state whether Luca notifies customers when sub-processors change.

parameters.name: Deletion and retention after you disconnect
parameters.definition: Retention and deletion rules set out how long a vendor keeps your data and when it is removed after you stop using the service.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is the vendor's stated timing for removing your data after you disconnect a platform or close your account.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Data from Google connections is deleted within 30 days of disconnecting.
For other data, Luca's privacy policy states how long it is retained after an account closes. Read those periods at ask-luca.com/privacy.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps you plan an exit and answer retention questions in a review using the vendor's stated periods.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Without stated rules, you could not tell how long your data stays with a vendor after you leave.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Finance leads, legal teams and anyone responsible for data retention policy.

parameters.example: Read the retention section of the privacy policy and note the period for each type of data you plan to connect. If you test a Google connection, record the date you disconnect and ask Luca's team to confirm when deletion is complete.
parameters.boundary: The 30-day deletion window applies to Google data after disconnecting. Retention for other data follows the periods in the privacy policy, which this page does not repeat.
parameters.review: Add the retention periods for other data from the privacy policy, and confirm whether customers can request earlier deletion.

parameters.name: Read-only access scopes
parameters.definition: An access scope is the set of permissions an app requests when you connect a platform. A read-only scope lets the app view data without changing it.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is the published list of permissions a vendor requests on each platform you connect.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca's privacy policy states that Google access is read-only and names the read-only Search Console scope, webmasters.readonly.
For other platforms, the scopes Luca requests are shown on that platform's own permission screen when you connect.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps you check what Luca can access on Google before you approve a connection, and supports a least-privilege review.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Without published scopes, you would rely on each permission screen alone and could not check access in advance.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Whoever approves platform connections, and reviewers checking access levels.

parameters.example: When you connect Search Console, check that the permission screen matches the read-only scope named in the privacy policy. For each other platform you connect, record the permissions its screen shows before you approve.
parameters.boundary: Published for Google connections; scopes for other connectors are shown on each platform's own permission screen.
parameters.review: Confirm whether Luca will publish scopes for each connector beyond Google, and attach screenshots of the permission screens.

parameters.name: Hosted on Google Cloud Platform
parameters.definition: Hosting describes the cloud infrastructure a service runs on.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is the infrastructure provider that runs the service and stores its data.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca's infrastructure runs on Google Cloud Platform, as stated in the privacy policy.
Customer data is stored there in separate BigQuery datasets, and credentials are kept in Google Secret Manager.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps you identify the infrastructure layer in a vendor review and apply any assessment you already hold of that provider.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Without knowing the host, you cannot assess the infrastructure layer of a vendor.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Security reviewers and IT leads.

parameters.example: Check that Google Cloud Platform appears in the privacy policy as both the infrastructure provider and a sub-processor. If your review needs more detail on hosting, ask Luca's team.
parameters.boundary: This names the hosting provider only. Ask Luca's team for any further hosting detail your review needs.
parameters.review: Confirm which hosting details, if any, Luca is willing to publish beyond the provider name.

parameters.name: Published pricing
parameters.definition: Published pricing means plans and prices are shown publicly, so you can read them without talking to sales.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is a vendor making its plans and prices public rather than sharing them only on a sales call.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca publishes its plans and prices on ask-luca.com/pricing, and you can read them there without a sales call.
This documentation describes the pricing model and does not repeat the figures.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps you check fit and budget before you speak to anyone at Luca.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Without published pricing, you would need a sales conversation just to learn whether Luca fits your budget.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Founders and finance leads in early evaluation.

parameters.example: Open ask-luca.com/pricing and choose the plan that fits the number of people who will use Luca. Compare that cost with what you spend today on analytics tools or analysis time.
parameters.boundary: Current figures are on ask-luca.com/pricing only. This page does not quote prices.
parameters.review: Confirm the pricing page is current, and link it from every pricing page in these docs.

parameters.name: Priced by seat
parameters.definition: Seat-based pricing charges for the number of people who use a product.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is a pricing model where cost follows the number of users rather than the size of the business.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca prices by seat. Your store revenue, order volume and ad spend do not set the price.
Current seat prices are on ask-luca.com/pricing.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps you predict cost from your team size rather than from your trading figures.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Where pricing is tied to revenue, orders or ad spend, your bill can change with your trading results, which makes budgeting harder.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Brands that want software cost tied to team size.

parameters.example: List the people who will use Luca, then use the seat prices on ask-luca.com/pricing to work out your cost. Ask Luca's team how adding or removing a seat is billed.
parameters.boundary: This describes how the price is calculated, not the price itself. Confirm what counts as a seat with Luca's team.
parameters.review: Confirm what counts as a seat and how seat changes are billed.

parameters.name: Price does not rise with your revenue
parameters.definition: A pricing model in which growth in revenue or orders does not increase what you pay.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It means your plan price stays the same as your sales grow.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Because Luca prices per seat, the plan price does not rise as your revenue or order volume grows.
What you pay follows your seats and plan, not your trading volume.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps you grow sales without your Luca cost rising with them.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: With revenue-linked pricing, a strong month or season could raise your bill.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Growing brands planning for higher volume.

parameters.example: Work out your cost at today's revenue and at your growth target using the seat prices on ask-luca.com/pricing. The two figures should differ only if you plan to add seats or change plan.
parameters.boundary: Your price can still change if you add seats or move plan. Check ask-luca.com/pricing for current figures.
parameters.review: Confirm whether any plan has limits, such as on stores or connections, that could require a change of plan.

parameters.name: Unlimited usage on every plan
parameters.definition: Unlimited usage means a plan does not cap or meter how much you use the product.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is a plan term that removes usage allowances, such as credits or question limits.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Every plan on ask-luca.com/pricing lists unlimited usage.
Seats, not usage, are the basis of the price.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps your team ask as many questions as the work needs without tracking an allowance.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: With metered or credit-based usage, teams often ration questions to control cost.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Teams that expect to use Luca often.

parameters.example: During setup or a trial, have each seat holder work through the questions they usually answer in a week. Then read the plan details on ask-luca.com/pricing to confirm that level of use does not change your cost.
parameters.boundary: This reflects what the pricing page lists. Read the plan details there for any usage terms.
parameters.review: Confirm whether any fair-use terms apply to unlimited usage.

parameters.name: No integration fees
parameters.definition: An integration fee is a charge for connecting a data source or building a custom connector.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is a commitment not to charge separately for connecting your systems.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca's website states that custom connectors carry no integration fee.
Luca's team handles custom connectors and integration mapping as part of onboarding.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps you connect systems that need a custom connector without a separate setup bill.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Where vendors charge per integration, connecting less common systems can add cost before you see any value.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Brands whose systems need a custom connector.

parameters.example: List the systems you use that may need a custom connector and raise them with Luca's team before onboarding. Ask them to confirm in writing that no integration fee applies to each one.
parameters.boundary: This covers integration fees for custom connectors. It does not set a timeline for building them; ask Luca's team.
parameters.review: Confirm the website wording and any limits on which custom connectors Luca's team will build.

parameters.name: Compared with hiring an analyst
parameters.definition: A way to judge a tool's cost against the cost of hiring a person to do similar work.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is a cost frame that compares software with the analysis work a team does by hand or would hire for.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca is positioned as doing the work of an analyst and advisor for a growing brand that cannot yet hire one.
You ask questions in plain English and Luca answers from your connected data and the reconciled view in Numbers.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps you weigh the cost of Luca against the analysis time your team spends today.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Without this frame, you may compare Luca only with other software and overlook the time your team spends on analysis.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Growing brands without an in-house analyst or advisor.

parameters.example: Write down the analysis questions your team answered by hand last month. Ask Luca the same questions during setup or a trial, and compare the answers and the time taken.
parameters.boundary: This is how Luca is positioned, not a guaranteed saving. Judge it against your own team's workload.
parameters.review: Confirm whether Luca wants to publish a cost comparison with hiring, and which sources it would use.

parameters.name: Annual billing discount
parameters.definition: An annual billing discount is a lower effective price for paying for a year at a time instead of monthly.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is a billing option that rewards a yearly commitment with a lower price than monthly billing.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca offers annual billing at a discount to monthly billing.
The size of the discount and the plan prices are shown on ask-luca.com/pricing.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps you lower your cost if you are ready to commit for a year.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Without an annual option, you would pay the monthly rate whatever your commitment.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Brands ready to commit to Luca for a year.

parameters.example: Compare the monthly and annual figures on ask-luca.com/pricing for your seat count. Before you choose, ask Luca's team how cancellation and seat changes work on annual billing.
parameters.boundary: This page does not state the discount. Check ask-luca.com/pricing for current terms.
parameters.review: Confirm annual terms, including cancellation and changes to seats during the term.

parameters.name: Card and data connection at signup
parameters.definition: Some products ask for payment details and a data connection when you create your account.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is a signup flow that collects card details and a first data connection at the start.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca's signup asks for a data connection and card details up front.
Signup also includes creating an organisation before you connect data.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: Connecting data at signup means your first look at Luca uses your own data.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Without a connection at signup, there would be nothing of yours to analyse until you added one later.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: The person setting up the account, usually a founder or operator.

parameters.example: Before you start signup, choose the first platform to connect and have the card you will bill to ready. Read the current trial and billing terms on ask-luca.com/pricing before you enter card details.
parameters.boundary: This page does not state trial length or when a card is charged. Confirm those on ask-luca.com/pricing.
parameters.review: Confirm the order of signup steps and whether the card is charged at signup or later, and attach screenshots.

parameters.name: Organisation setup during signup
parameters.definition: Organisation setup is the signup step where you create the account that represents your business before adding data.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is the first part of signup, where your business is set up in the product.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Signup includes creating an organisation before you connect data.
Once the organisation exists, you move on to connecting your data.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps keep your data connections set up under your business from the start.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Without an organisation step, there would be no clear account for your brand's connections to sit under.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: The person creating the account.

parameters.example: When you sign up, create the organisation for the brand you are evaluating, then connect one data source. Ask Luca's team how to add colleagues if you need them.
parameters.boundary: This page does not describe organisation settings, multi-brand setups or user roles. Ask Luca's team about those.

parameters.name: Hands-on onboarding with Luca's team
parameters.definition: Hands-on onboarding means the vendor's team does much of the setup work with you, rather than leaving you to configure the product alone.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is an onboarding service where the vendor's people do significant setup work for each client.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca's team does significant onboarding work for each client.
Because of this, Luca manages how many new clients it onboards at a time, so each one gets that support.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps you start with your systems set up by people who know the product, without your team doing all the configuration.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: With self-serve setup only, your team would carry the mapping and configuration work itself.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Brands without spare analyst or engineering time for setup.

parameters.example: Before signing up, ask Luca's team which intake you would join and what they need from you. During onboarding, note which tasks the team handled and which fell to you.
parameters.boundary: Onboarding capacity is managed by intake, so your start date depends on availability. This page does not set timelines; ask Luca's team.
parameters.review: Confirm the onboarding steps and typical duration, and decide whether to publish onboarding availability.

parameters.name: Data mapping done by Luca's team
parameters.definition: Data mapping is matching fields and records across systems so that figures from different sources line up.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is the work of making data from separate systems agree, so a combined view can be trusted.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca's team handles custom connectors and integration mapping for you.
The team also reconciles your systems into Numbers, Luca's reconciled view of your figures.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps you get a consistent view across your sales, advertising, payments and accounting data without your team doing the mapping.

answers.question: What happens without it?
paragraphs: Without vendor mapping, your team would need to work out how each system's figures relate before relying on a combined view.

answers.question: Who is it for?
paragraphs: Brands with several connected systems and no in-house data team.

parameters.example: Pick a figure you already reconcile by hand, such as one month's revenue across your store and your accounting system. Once Luca's team has completed the mapping, compare it with Numbers and raise any differences with them.
parameters.boundary: Mapping is done by Luca's team as part of onboarding. This page does not describe self-serve mapping.
parameters.review: Confirm the mapping steps and what the client reviews or signs off, and attach a screenshot of Numbers.

parameters.name: Luca community
parameters.definition: A customer community is a shared space where users and prospects exchange ideas about a product.

answers.question: What is it?
paragraphs: It is a place to learn from other people using the same product.

answers.question: How does it work in Luca?
paragraphs: Luca runs a community for clients and prospects on Heartbeat. You can reach it at community.ask-luca.com or through the Heartbeat apps for iOS and Android.
Members exchange prompts, workflows and use cases.

answers.question: How does it help?
paragraphs: This helps you see how other brands ask questions of Luca and adapt their workflows to your own.

answers.question: What happens without it?
